narrative.summary: In the isolated village of Little Middleton, the respected village elder Beatrice Dunmore is found murdered in the archaeological dig site office. An official excavation report, accepted unquestioningly by the village’s authorities, is taken as proof that Beatrice discovered a secret weeks before her death. However, Detective Frances Orme uncovers that the report’s provenance was forged by the dig supervisor Ambrose Rutherford, manipulating the village’s trust in archival authority to conceal the truth. The case unravels through careful document analysis and witness testimonies, culminating in a test exposing the forged record and revealing the real time of death.

The report was accepted by villagers and authorities as genuine

Archival stamps appear on the report indicating filing dates

inferred_conclusions: The excavation report's date was forged by tampering with ink aging

mechanism.description: Ambrose Rutherford applied a chemical treatment to the ink on the excavation report to simulate natural oxidation, fooling visual inspection and basic ink solubility tests. This forged the report's date to appear as three weeks old, while the paper's watermark and archival stamps show a manufacture date six months later and filing inconsistencies. The village's unquestioning trust in archival authority led to acceptance of the forged report, which was used to misplace the timeline of Beatrice Dunmore's discovery and death, delaying suspicion of Rutherford until Frances Orme's investigation exposed the forgery.

false_assumption.what_it_hides: The report was chemically forged with ink artificially aged, and archival stamps were falsified to conceal the true date, misleading the timeline of the victim’s death and discovery.

discriminating_test.design: Compare the archival filing order and paper watermark dates with the excavation report's ink aging; subject Ambrose Rutherford to chemical ink aging tests on the report and test his knowledge of chemical treatments applicable in the 1930s archival context to prove forgery.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: Demonstrates that only Ambrose Rutherford had the access, chemical knowledge, and authority to forge the excavation report, falsifying the timeline and implicating him in the murder.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The chemical ink aging test confirms artificial aging inconsistent with archival standards, and archival stamp order confirms report backdating.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1 uses archival stamps and paper watermark to expose date contradictions; Step 2 uses physical traces on the letter opener to eliminate Ottoline; Step 3 uses ink aging comparisons to identify forgery by Ambrose; Step 4 uses alibi timing to link Ambrose to the murder act. All clues are introduced before the discriminating test and are concrete, observable facts accessible to the reader.
